messages.content: You are helping a publishing production and legal-review coordinator keep an accurate manuscript record. Distinguish confirmed passage statuses from proposed edits, apply the stated queue-eligibility rule literally, and do not claim to have redacted text, contacted the author, or made any legal determination yourself.

I am tracking pre-publication legal review for the manuscript Low Tide at Cortes together with Renata from rights and Devon from production. Our queue-eligibility rule is deliberately simple, and I want it recorded before we apply it to anything: a manuscript is eligible for the fast-track queue only if, at the close of legal review, at most three passages remain flagged, and none of those remaining flagged passages names a living private individual by full name. If either condition fails, more passages remain flagged than that, or any remaining flagged passage names a living private individual by full name, the manuscript takes the standard queue instead. This is a conjunctive gate, not a general risk judgment, and I do not want it applied until the passage-level evidence is in the record.

Understood. I will treat this as a two-part gate: the count of passages still flagged at the close of review must be three or fewer, and none of those flagged passages may name a living private individual by full name. Both conditions must hold for the fast-track queue; failing either one is sufficient to require the standard queue. I will wait for the confirmed passage-level evidence before naming a queue, and I will keep each passage's naming status as a separate observation rather than inferring it from the others.

Renata's review has narrowed the flagged list to exactly three passages; no further passages are under review. Passage one quotes a public agency's press release verbatim and names no individual, living or otherwise, so it was cleared without any edit. Passage two originally named a source directly, but the tracked manuscript file now refers to that person only as a former dockworker, with no name anywhere in the passage; Devon confirmed this rewrite is already merged into the working file, not a proposed diff. Both statuses come from the current manuscript file and Renata's review notes, not from a draft or a verbal summary.

I have passage one and passage two recorded as confirmed and cleared of naming a living private individual, based on the current manuscript file and Renata's review notes. That leaves passage three as the only one of the three flagged passages whose naming status is still open, and I will treat it as a separate observation rather than assuming it matches the other two.

Passage three has been confirmed redacted. The manuscript file now reads name withheld at legal's request at the point where the individual was previously identified, and Renata verified that redaction against the current file, not a draft.

I have passage three recorded as a separate observation from passages one and two, exactly as reported. I will use the strict wording of the queue rule only when you ask for the queue decision directly, and I will not state a queue in this message.

Separately, the audio rights have already been settled and are not part of the legal-review gate. The audiobook edition of Low Tide at Cortes will be produced by Meridian Audio, and that vendor assignment is independent of the legal-review queue; it will not change if the queue assignment changes.

Recorded as a separate control fact: Meridian Audio is confirmed for the audiobook narration, independent of the legal-review queue decision. I will not infer the vendor assignment from the queue, or the queue from the vendor assignment.

Before we go further, give me a procedural checklist for what Devon should verify before treating the production handoff as complete for this title. Keep it procedural: identify where each confirmed passage status is logged, who owns any item that is still open, and how a superseded instruction should be marked so it is not silently replaced. Do not invent ticket numbers, page numbers, or say that any check has been performed that is not already documented above.

Devon should verify that each passage-level claim points to its evidence location, such as the manuscript file diff or Renata's review notes; that any still-open item names an owner and a next check date; and that an outdated instruction is visibly marked as superseded rather than silently replaced or deleted. The handoff should separate confirmed observations, settled production assignments, and open questions, so a later reader can immediately see which claims are settled and which are still pending.

The copyediting team will inherit this discussion once the file is handed off. Suggest a compact structure for that handoff note that does not repeat any settled legal-review outcome or the narration-vendor assignment. It should still make clear how a new observation can be added later without erasing the earlier record.

Use four short sections: current context, evidence references, open items with owners, and a change log. Put each new observation in the change log with its source and date, then link it to any open item it affects. If a new note supersedes an earlier one, preserve the old entry and label the relationship explicitly rather than deleting it. This keeps the handoff auditable without restating any settled detail.

Renata also asked how to flag uncertainty when a review result is delayed, for instance if a fact-checker's response has not arrived yet. We need wording that distinguishes a missing observation from a failed check, because the copyediting team should not treat silence as evidence of a problem. What labels would be clear without sounding bureaucratic?

Three plain labels should suffice: observed for a result backed by evidence already in the file or notes, pending when the expected observation has not arrived yet, and failed only when a completed check actually produced an adverse result. Put the expected source and the next review date beside any pending item. That keeps an absence of data visibly distinct from a real failure.

Give me a neutral sentence the handoff note can place above the open-items list. It should invite the copyediting team to verify the record, but it must not imply that Renata's team already completed work that is not documented here.
Continue from the documented evidence below, verify any item whose status is pending, and record new observations with their source before changing an existing conclusion.

One more procedural question: how should the proofing calendar note a passage that was re-flagged after an earlier pass cleared it, so the schedule does not look like it silently reopened without explanation?

Add a single calendar entry that names the passage, cites the reason it was re-flagged, and links back to the earlier clearance entry instead of overwriting it. Mark the earlier entry as superseded rather than removing it, so the schedule shows the full sequence: cleared, re-flagged, and the reason, in that order.
Last item: what belongs in the indexing and metadata note so it does not accidentally reference a passage's earlier wording after any redaction or edit is finalized?

The indexing note should reference passages by their stable passage identifier rather than by quoted text, so an index entry survives a later redaction or rewrite without edit. Any metadata field that does quote a passage directly should carry a last-verified date and be regenerated whenever that passage's status changes, rather than being treated as permanent.

focal.rule_or_relation: The fast-track queue requires at most three flagged passages at close of review, none naming a living private individual by full name; otherwise the standard queue is required.
focal.changed_input: The one load-bearing input is passage three's naming status: redacted in C versus naming Marta Coelho by full name in W.
focal.probe: Under the recorded queue-eligibility rule, which queue applies to Low Tide at Cortes? Answer with only the queue name.
focal.why_derived: The answer requires combining the fixed flagged-passage count of three, the cleared status of passages one and two, and passage three's naming status, then applying the conjunctive gate; no message states the queue directly.
focal.why_counterfactual_reverses: Changing only passage three from redacted to naming a living private individual by full name breaks the no-named-individual condition while the count stays at three, so the rule reverses the applicable queue.

nonfocal_control.probe: Which vendor was confirmed for the audiobook narration? Answer with only the vendor name.
nonfocal_control.why_independent_of_focal: The narration vendor assignment is a separately settled production fact and is explicitly independent of the legal-review queue rule.

distractor_fact_inventory.summary: Procedural checklist for evidence logs, owners, superseded notes, and an auditable change log for the production handoff.
Neutral terminology for observed, pending, and failed items plus a noncommittal handoff sentence.
Procedural notes for re-flagged passages on the proofing calendar and stable-identifier indexing after redaction.
